data.long_meaning: Derived from Old Norse, Erikson means 'ruler of the army of the gods'. This strong name conveys leadership and strength. The name Erikson carries the meaning “Ruler of the army of the gods” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Erikson usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of the army of the gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: אריקסון
in_hebrew.meaning: אל המלך הנצחי בנו של אריק
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אריקסון הוא שם פטרונומי שמשמעותו בנו של אריק, המורכב מהשם אריק וסיומת הבן -סון. אריק מקורו בשם העברי אריה או אריק, שפירושו שליט נצחי או אל מלך. השם אריקסון משמש לעתים קרובות בקהילות יהודיות ונוצריות כאחד, ומשדר חוזק ואצילות.

in_greek.name: Ερίκσον
in_greek.long_meaning: Το Ερίκσον είναι πατρωνυμικό όνομα που σημαίνει γιος του Ερικ, αποτελούμενο από το όνομα Ερικ και την κατάληξη -σον. Το Ερικ προέχεται από το εβραϊκό όνομα אריה או אריק, που σημαίνει αιώνιος κυβερνήτης ή θεός-βασιλιάς. Το Ερίκσον χρησιμοποιείται συχνά και στις κοινότητες των Εβραίων και των Χριστιανών, και ακτινοβολεί δύναμη και ευγένεια.

in_latin.name: Erikson
in_latin.long_meaning: Erikson is a patronymic name meaning son of Eric, derived from Eric and the suffix -son. Eric originates from the Hebrew name אריה or אריק, meaning eternal ruler or god-king. Erikson has been used in both Jewish and Christian communities, symbolizing strength and nobility.

in_english.name: Erikson
in_english.meaning: son of Eric, eternal ruler or noble leader
in_english.long_meaning: Erikson is a patronymic surname and given name meaning 'son of Eric.' The name Eric originates from the Old Norse name 'Eiríkr,' which is derived from the Proto-Germanic 'Einhariz' and the Old Norse 'ei,' meaning 'ever' or 'always,' and 'ríkr,' meaning 'ruler' or 'king.' This etymology connects Erikson to the Hebrew and Greek roots signifying eternal or forever. Historically, the name Erikson has been prevalent in Scandinavian countries and has been adopted into various Christian cultures. It signifies a legacy of leadership, strength, and eternal devotion.

data.cultural_impact: The name Erikson carries Norse heritage and emphasizes power and bravery, reflecting the legacy of Viking warriors. In the Christian context, it can symbolize a leader who upholds righteousness and protects their community, invoking images of both biblical kings and great historical figures.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Erik the Red was a Norse chieftain who discovered Greenland in the late 10th century. The name Erikson carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
Erik the Red's son, Leif Erikson, is believed to have been the first European to reach North America, around 1000 AD.
